Definition: from G473 and G4754; (figuratively) to attack, i.e. (by implication) destroy:--war against.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says he sees another law in his members, warring against the law of his mind and bringing him into captivity to the law of sin. The word is the war itself, the inner battle between the two laws.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for an inner war carries no doctrine of its own; its honesty is Paul's, that the law of sin still fights the law of the mind in every believer.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
